payload.name: Preserve prior facts when adding later event
payload.description: When a new message describes a later, distinct event about the same subject or project as an existing memory, avoid overwriting the existing memory. Add a new memory for the new event unless it directly revises the old facts.
content: If a later message references the same subject/project as an existing memory but describes a distinct event or state change (e.g., a completed item was later shown/used), do not overwrite the existing memory's content or dates.

Preserve the original durable facts and create a separate memory for the new event with its own world_start date; only UPDATE the existing memory when the new message explicitly contradicts or revises those original facts.
When extracting candidates, treat a later related mention as a new event candidate, not as a replacement for the earlier event, unless the earlier facts are expressly incorrect.

solves: When a user later reports a follow-up event about the same subject or project (e.g., an item was displayed, used, or shown after earlier completion), the Construction Agent may mistakenly UPDATE the existing memory, deleting earlier durable facts that remain true and are still needed to answer questions about the earlier period. This skill prevents loss of prior facts by requiring a separate memory for each distinct event unless the new message directly contradicts the old facts.
